title: 6 BORING Home-Based Businesses Anyone Can Run (Customers Mail You the Work)

stated_problem.quote: Because the VCR in the house died years ago and the footage exists nowhere else.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Home media digitization
idea.one_liner: Families mail old tapes, slides, and photos to a home operator who converts them to digital files and charges per item or by footage time.
idea.customer: Families with old home movies, slides, and photos they want preserved.
idea.offer: Mail-in conversion of home media to digital files, with originals returned.
idea.revenue_model: Per tape, per hour of footage, or per photo/slide transfer; optional related media services.

key_quotes.quote: Turning old home movies, slides, and photos into digital files.
Small independent operators on Reddit's data hoarder forum report charging $ 20 to $30 a tape.
A general price guide puts the typical range at 25 to35 for up to 2 hours of footage.
If you ran 15 tapes a week at $25, that's about $1,600 a month.
That's exactly where Harry started.
A handful of boxes from people who already know you, then referrals, then strangers who found you online.
A 2-hour tape and a 10-minute tape are not the same job.

ideas.delivery: The customer mails tapes, slides, or photos to the operator's home workspace. The operator digitizes them, sends an estimate for approval where needed, and returns the originals with the files.

stated_problem.quote: Then they pay that stranger to send it back whole.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Teddy bear repair
idea.one_liner: Owners mail damaged childhood bears to a specialist who repairs them and charges for the time and restoration work.
idea.customer: People with damaged childhood bears or other treasured stuffed animals.
idea.offer: Mail-in repair, quoted after photos and a repair list are reviewed.
idea.revenue_model: Hourly or half-hour pricing with a minimum charge per job.

key_quotes.quote: Teddy bear repair.
People put a childhood bear in a box and mail it to a stranger.
A stuffed animal repair listing on Etsy charges $20 per half hour with a minimum of 2 and 1/2 hours.
The customer is paying for a memory, not for stuffing.

claims.claim: An Etsy stuffed-animal repair listing charges $20 per half hour with a 2.5-hour minimum.
claims.quote: A stuffed animal repair listing on Etsy charges $20 per half hour with a minimum of 2 and 1/2 hours.

claims.claim: The smallest job at that minimum is $100.
claims.quote: So the smallest job is $100.

claims.claim: Getting started with a sewing machine, needles, thread, and stuffing is said to cost a few hundred at most.
claims.quote: Usually a basic sewing machine, needles, thread, and fresh stuffing, a few hundred at most.

claims.claim: Three jobs per week at the $100 minimum would hypothetically bring in about $1,300 per month.
claims.quote: Three jobs a week at that $100 minimum is about $1,300 a month.

claims.claim: The Etsy listing offers a turnaround transcribed as “twoe”; the duration is unclear in the transcript.
claims.quote: That Etsy listing even offers a twoe turnaround, which tells you something.

acquisition_channels.details: Etsy listings are cited, and Etsy is suggested as a place to start.
Local parent groups are suggested.
Before-and-after bear photos are suggested as shareable promotion.

ideas.delivery: The owner mails a bear to the repairer. The repairer reviews photos and a repair list, quotes the job, repairs it by hand, then mails it back.

prices: about $1,300 a month at three jobs a week

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to customer contact details and any identifiable photos retained. Consumer Rights Act 2015 and Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 may apply to remote consumer service orders.

stated_problem.quote: The joystick that moves on its own.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Controller repair, especially joystick drift
idea.one_liner: Gamers mail controllers with drifting sticks to a repairer who replaces the sticks and charges per repair.
idea.customer: Players with joystick drift, especially those who want to keep a particular controller.
idea.offer: Mail-in controller inspection and stick replacement, including Hall effect stick upgrades.
idea.revenue_model: Flat repair pricing per stick or controller, with shipping charged or arranged separately.

key_quotes.quote: The third business fixes the most annoying problem in gaming, controller drift.
Ties controller repair in Hamilton, Ontario takes mail and jobs from across Canada.
A single stick drift repair is $20 with the new stick included and the range runs 20 to35.
Customers live in gaming groups, Reddit threads, and Discord servers.

claims.claim: Ties charges $20 for a single stick drift repair with the new stick included; the stated range is 20 to 35.
claims.quote: A single stick drift repair is $20 with the new stick included and the range runs 20 to35.

claims.claim: Round-trip shipping starts at $5 and usual turnaround is about 24 hours.
claims.quote: Roundtrip shipping starts at $5 and the usual turnaround is about 24 hours.

claims.claim: Home Tech Center lists both sticks at £45.
claims.quote: In the UK, Home Tech Center lists both sticks at £45.

claims.claim: Stick Fix Repair sends customers a free mail-in kit and charges a flat rate.
claims.quote: In the US, Stick Fix Repair sends customers a free mail in kit and charges a flat rate.

claims.claim: A hobbyist listed parts costing about $20 for a soldering iron, $7 for desoldering ribbon, and $10 for two Hall effect sticks.
claims.quote: About $20 for a soldering iron, $7 for desoldering ribbon, and $10 for two Hall effect sticks.

claims.claim: The narrator estimates each stick costs about $5 against a repair selling for 20 to 35.
claims.quote: That's about $5 a stick on a repair that sells for 20 to 35.

claims.claim: At 15 repairs a week and about $30 each, hypothetical monthly revenue is about $1,900.
claims.quote: If you did 15 repairs a week at around $30, that's about $1,900 a month.

claims.claim: Ties is said to turn most jobs around in about a day.
claims.quote: Ties turns most jobs in about a day.

claims.claim: The narrator says the first stick replacement feels slow and the tenth is routine.
claims.quote: The first stick replacement feels slow. By the 10th, it's routine.

claims.claim: The narrator says the fiftieth repair becomes muscle memory.
claims.quote: And the 50th is muscle memory.

acquisition_channels.details: Post before-and-after repair videos in gaming groups and on social platforms.
Reddit threads, Discord servers, and local gaming groups are suggested.
The suggested start is to repair one's own controller, then a friend's, then take jobs from a local group.

ideas.delivery: Customers mail in controllers, or receive a mail-in label or kit. The repairer logs serial numbers, photographs each arrival, replaces the stick by hand, and ships the controller back.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to customer contact details and identifiable information linked to controller serial numbers. Consumer Rights Act 2015 and Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 may apply to remote consumer service orders.

stated_problem.quote: The fourth business turns dirty sneakers into a line of customers.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Sneaker cleaning and restoration
idea.one_liner: Sneaker owners mail or drop off dirty or collectible shoes for cleaning and restoration, paying by service tier.
idea.customer: Sneaker owners, especially people with limited releases or collectible shoes.
idea.offer: Cleaning and restoration, with inspection before the final quote and mail-in or local drop-off options.
idea.revenue_model: Tiered per-pair cleaning and restoration fees, with add-ons such as sole icing.

key_quotes.quote: Sneaker cleaning and restoration.
Sneaky Clean lists a signature clean at $34.99 and a premium clean at $49.99.
Operators swapping prices on Reddit's sneaker cleaning form land around 25 for a clean and about 10 more for icing the souls.

stated_problem.quote: One town might have only a handful of people with a falling apart family Bible.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Bible and book rebinding
idea.one_liner: Families mail worn Bibles and books to a bookbinder who repairs or rebinds them, charging by the type and extent of work.
idea.customer: Families, churches, and genealogy groups with worn Bibles or valued books.
idea.offer: Mail-in repair and rebinding, including leather covers, repairs, and restoration of family Bibles.
idea.revenue_model: Per-book pricing by binding type, materials, and repair scope.

key_quotes.quote: Bible and book rebinding.
A full rebind in genuine leather runs $150 to $175.
Why would someone pay $200 to fix a book they could replace for a fraction of that?
Because the Family Bible holds the names.
Customers come through churches, genealogy groups, and families settling in a state.

claims.quote: A full rebind in genuine leather runs $150 to $175. A pocket Bible is 100.

claims.claim: An inlay binding costs 200 and minor repairs start at 25.
claims.quote: An inlay binding is 200 and minor repairs start at 25.

claims.quote: Leonard's Book Restoration in Burroughs, Indiana takes Bibles by mail, and a customer review from 2013 put a standard rebind there at about $200.

claims.claim: A small press, hand tools, and good leather are said to cost well under a couple of thousand.
claims.quote: A small press, a few hand tools, and good leather can usually be gathered for well under a couple of thousand.

claims.claim: Three rebinds per week at 150 would hypothetically bring in close to $2,000 per month.
claims.quote: Three rebinds a week at 150 is close to $2,000 a month.

claims.claim: One finished Bible shared in a Sunday school class is said to bring the next three customers.
claims.quote: One finished Bible passed around a Sunday school class can bring the next three.

claims.quote: Plan on months of practice rather than weeks, starting on thrift store hard covers before anyone hands you a family heirloom.

acquisition_channels.details: Churches, genealogy groups, and Sunday school classes are named as sources of customers.
A finished Bible shared in a class may bring additional customers.
Leonard's Book Restoration is cited as a mail-in example.

ideas.delivery: Customers mail books or Bibles to a home workshop. The binder removes worn covers, repairs loose pages, rebinds the original text block, and returns the book.

prices: well under a couple of thousand startup
